subject: science
title: Make It Move
about: What a push or pull does to a thing: starts it, stops it, turns it, and how a harder or gentler force changes how fast and far it goes (PS.1.1.1, PS.1.1.2). Includes magnets pulling without touching.
tip: Race a toy car with a soft push and a hard push and ask him to predict which goes farther before each try.

cards.q: A force is a push or a...
cards.note: Forces make things start, stop, speed up, slow down or turn.

cards.q: You push a ball that is sitting still. What happens?
You catch a rolling ball. What happens to it?
A ball comes to you. You hit it with a bat. What changes?
cards.note: A push can send a thing a new way.

cards.q: You push a toy car hard. How does it go?
You push the same toy car gently. How does it go?
Which kick sends a ball farther?
A ball sits still. Nobody pushes or pulls it. What does it do?
You pull a sled. Then you pull harder. What happens?
A rolling ball bumps into a block. What happens to the block?
cards.note: Things can push things, not just people.

cards.q: What can pull a paper clip without touching it?
Which one does a magnet pull?
cards.note: Magnets pull some metals, like iron and steel, not paper, wood or plastic.

cards.q: How does a magnet move a paper clip?
Same car, same floor, two pushes. One time it went farther. What was different?
You want to know which push makes the car go farther. What do you do?
A ball rolls slowly. You push it from behind. What happens?
